{"type":"text","timestamp":1794628992065,"sessionID":"ses_e27c86834ffekdoitLepIEuA3Z","part":{"id":"prt_1d8393bf5001QFhgrHIt4yKER5","messageID":"msg_1d8391727001Q85x4lOAkgw2cy","sessionID":"ses_e27c86834ffekdoitLepIEuA3Z","type":"text","text":"The episode is over. The rover sampled all 5 initial targets on time, worth 7 points. It ended at base with about 13.6 battery left, so I expect a score of about **7/10 = 0.70**. The episode doesn't show the final score, so 0.70 is my estimate.\n\n**Base return:** the final position is an estimate, not a confirmed fact, because each position report has about 0.3 m of noise. Averaging the reports after the last correction puts the rover at roughly (20.04, 20.16), about 0.17 m from base (20, 20). That is well inside the 0.75 m radius.\n\n**Missed target:** I didn't sample the one target that appeared mid-mission, d1 (worth 3, deadline tick 33). I only learned about it at tick 25, and the drive to t1 was already queued and couldn't be cancelled. After t1, there was no plan the battery could cover that would beat 7 points:\n- **t1 → d1 → base:** needed about 40 battery with only about 33 left, so the rover would have run dry and scored 0.\n- **Stop at d1:** (7 + 3) × 0.5 = 5, which is less than 7.\n- **From base, a round trip to d1:** cost about 19 battery against about 12 spare.\n\nNo second discovery appeared.\n\n**How it went:**\n- **Timing:** commands took effect 4 ticks after sending. To save time, I queued each leg's two drives and the sample straight away rather than waiting for telemetry first.\n- **Heading drift:** the rover's actual path ran about 3.3° clockwise of the commanded heading. I measured this on the first two legs and corrected every later heading for it.\n- **Wheel slip:** bedrock slip is 0–5%, so I made each drive 2.5% longer than the planned distance.\n- **Final correction:** after reaching base, I averaged 10 position reports taken while the rover was still. That showed it about 0.45 m short, so I sent one 0.43 m drive to close the gap.\n\n**What would have done better:** each tick cost 0.5 battery even when the rover sat still. Sending the next leg the moment the last drive finished, instead of leaving idle ticks, would have kept enough battery to go for d1 as well.","time":{"start":1794628991989,"end":1794628992064}}}
